Checklist Item: HTML validates without errors
Comments: HTML tidy validation reveals two categories of issues: (1) <sly> tag errors — these are AEM/HTL-specific template tags that tidy does not recognise as valid HTML. This is expected in AEM HTL components and not a true HTML error (sly elements are stripped at render time). Missing DOCTYPE in component fragments is also expected in AEM (DOCTYPE is in the page template). The unescaped & in URL attributes is a genuine HTML validation error.

Checklist Item: ARIA roles do not duplicate native semantics
Comments: Two categories of ARIA role issues: (1) Redundant roles — <button role='button'> found 6 times in cards-compare.html — the button element already has implicit role='button'; this is unnecessary but harmless. (2) role='button' on <a> elements in exit-intent-popup.html, video-filter.html, and others — technically these override the native 'link' role and may cause AT confusion. role='tablist', 'tabpanel', 'tab', 'group', 'region', 'menu', 'alert' usages on divs/sections are appropriate since those elements have no native semantic equivalent.

Checklist Item: Avoid misuse of ARIA roles
Comments: Multiple ARIA role misuses: (1) role='menu' on dropdown filter divs (blog-filter.html:54, searchandlogin.html:179, header-help-section.html:15) — role='menu' is for application-context menus (like context menus), not navigation dropdowns. Should use role='list' or role='group'. (2) role='presentation' on images with non-empty alt text (searchandlogin.html:8,13,206, blog-grid.html:22) — conflicting attributes; presentation removes the semantic role including the alt text from AT. (3) <datalist role='listbox'> in cards-compare.html — datalist already has implicit listbox semantics; the explicit role is redundant. (4) role='combobox' on plain input element with datalist is partially valid but requires additional ARIA properties (aria-expanded, aria-haspopup).

Comments: 239 box-shadow declarations found. Checklist Item: Avoid memory leaks
Comments: Significant memory leak risk: 415 addEventListener calls vs only 7 removeEventListener calls across all component JS files. This ~59:1 ratio indicates event listeners are rarely cleaned up. In an AEM SPA/component model, if components are dynamically added/removed from the DOM (e.g., via editor overlays, lazy loading, AJAX navigation), event listeners attached to elements or to document/window will persist as memory leaks. Additionally, setInterval in steps-tp-apply.js has no clearInterval on component destroy. Observer usage (IntersectionObserver, ResizeObserver) also lacks verified disconnect() cleanup. Without a component lifecycle destroy() method that calls removeEventListener, listeners on long-lived elements (document, window, header) accumulate.

Checklist Item: Event listeners cleaned up properly
Comments: Event listeners are not properly cleaned up. As established in Row 62: 415 addEventListener vs only 7 removeEventListener calls (ratio ~59:1).
